title: Leptos
notes: Leptos pages rendered on the server through leptos_axum; the API is an axum route. Server only: no client bundle is built. Its pages carry <!> hydration markers, which the comparison drops.
details: A Leptos application rendered on the server through leptos_axum (the layout of the start-axum template): the shell, Leptos's own router for /about and /items/:id, and components written with view!; values are escaped by Leptos. Its server-rendered pages carry <!> hydration placeholders after each rendered list and in place of an absent optional element, which the page comparison drops as it does comments. /api/items/:id is an axum route with axum's Json on the same router, which is how Leptos's documentation serves an endpoint with an address of its own (a server function is a POST to a generated address). /about is rendered on each request; Leptos's static routes were not used. Built with plain cargo build --release, without cargo-leptos: only the server is built, so the hydration script the pages reference (/pkg/*.js and .wasm) is not built or served, and no page needs it. The options are built in main (LeptosOptions::builder with an output name) because cargo-leptos is not there to pass them, and the listener is bound to a free port instead of the site address; otherwise the defaults are kept (out-of-order streaming SSR, no compression). Manual version pins, all because the newest releases were under seven days old on 2026-10-07: leptos =0.8.21 (0.8.22 was two days old) and leptos_router =0.8.16 (0.8.17) in Cargo.toml, and in Cargo.lock leptos_macro 0.8.18 (0.8.19), server_fn_macro 0.8.11 (0.8.12), server_fn_macro_default 0.8.5 (0.8.6), hydration_context 0.3.1 (0.3.2) and leptos_hot_reload 0.8.6 (0.8.7). One process on Tokio's default multi-threaded runtime (one worker thread per core), at Cargo's default release settings. Cargo cannot skip build scripts or procedural macros, so those of the locked crates run at build time, as for every Rust entry here.
